messages:
support-ops: Hey all — multiple customers reporting 503s starting ~09:03 UTC. Volume spike on hosted model 'redwood-7b-v1' routes. CS getting angry. Attaching logs.
cs-rep: Customer ACME says requests time out, repeated 503s. They sent a couple of request IDs.
oncall-infra: Looking at metrics — host group infer-pool-4 has a restart spike across 3 containers, CPU fine, GPU memory usage shows abrupt jumps then OOM kill.
eng-runtime: Can you paste the worker logs? suspecting a kv-prefetch/kv-cache race during cold-cache prefetch. Also have we recently rolled quantized binaries?
support-ops: Paste log snippet from a failed run: ```
[2026-03-17T09:02:58Z] runner[pid=12233] ERROR: segfault at 0x7f8a...
[stack] 0x00007f8a kernel::attn::compute +0x1a2
[2026-03-17T09:03:01Z] runtime: 1 process exit status=139
NVIDIA: GPU 0: out of memory during allocate 2048MB
```
eng-sre: Container restarts look like CrashLoopBackOff, restart_count > 15 on three pods. Kube shows OOMKilled on the runtime side before segfault in native lib. Could be a memory spike during prefetch.
eng-ml: We pushed the quant-swap heuristic yesterday to reduce mem for long context. There's a path where quant swap + prefetch spikes transient allocations — I've seen this in local repro.
oncall-infra: Repro steps? can we reproduce in staging with same q/s config and prefetch enabled?
eng-ml: Steps: run streaming requests with context ~12k tokens, enable prefetch=true, model variant=redwood-7b-v1-q4. On my rig it triggered a cudaMalloc failure after 30-40 prefetched contexts.
eng-runtime: Good. For immediate mitigation we should do fallback routing for affected customer routes to the lower-memory model variant (v1-cpu-fallback or v1-q2). Also disable prefetch on that route if possible.
product-ts: CS — what's the impact window and which customers affected? Need to coordinate customer comms.
cs-rep: Impacted: ACME, BetaApp, and two smaller accounts. They saw 10-70% increased 503s between 09:03-09:18.
support-ops: I've already opened a priority support ticket and offered a temporary key-level rate limit to reduce concurrency. Waiting for approval to route them to fallback.
eng-sre: I'm applying a temporary node drain on pool infer-pool-4 and re-scheduling workloads to infer-pool-2. Also bumping pod memory request + limit on a canary to see if it holds (will monitor).
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] rolling update started: runtime/image:2026-03-16-quant-fix -> runtime/image:2026-03-17-hotfix-canary (canary=1/10)
eng-runtime: Please attach the core dump and a device trace. If segfault persists after increasing mem limit, we need an emergency rollback of the quant-swap change.
eng-ml: I'll reproduce with the exact workload and try a build with a guard around the prefetch path. If we can trigger locally, will push a fix.
product-ts: CS and support-ops — draft of customer note: "We're investigating intermittent 503s for some model requests; as a temporary measure we are routing affected traffic to a lower-memory model and applying rate-limits. We expect restoration within the hour." ok?
cs-rep: Ok — send now, they'll want ETA.
support-ops: Message sent. ACME responded: thanks, please keep us posted — they are on a demo at 10:00.
eng-sre: Short-term: disabled prefetch per-route for ACME and BetaApp, forced fallback routing to v1-q2. Observability: 503s for those clients dropped to baseline in ~90s.
oncall-infra: Good. Continue to watch for other pools. I'm creating a playbook entry for this pattern (cold-cache prefetch + quant swap -> transient alloc spike -> OOM -> segfault).
eng-runtime: Next actions: (1) collect core+nvprof from affected hosts, (2) revert quant-swap on prod if canary shows issues, (3) add a guard to prefetch to cap concurrent allocs, (4) synthetic test for long-context prefetch load.
eng-ml: I'll prioritize a fix for prefetch allocator and push unit/regression tests.
product-ts: Keep CS posted every 15m. If rollback needed, get sign-off from Eng lead + Ops.
support-ops: Recording incident. Severity: P2 (customer-facing, partial outage). Will escalate to P1 if more customers fail.
eng-sre: Notes: actioned fallback routing, patched mem limits, drained node. Leaving one canary with higher limits to gather more traces.
eng-runtime: Thanks — once we have core dumps I'll run ASAN builds against it. If kernel shows a pointer into quant lib we rollback.
eng-ml: Patch in progress, will push review in ~45min.
cs-rep: ACME confirms demo can proceed with routing change. Closing immediate customer escalation.
product-ts: Great. Keep this thread updated with root cause & follow-ups for postmortem. :thumbsup:
